newsitem.title: TURKEY: FOCUS-Turkish govt hopes fuel shares leap to record high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Turkish govt hopes fuel shares leap to record high.

text.p: Turkish shares smashed through record highs on Friday with a gain of over six percent, fuelled by rising hopes for a secularist coalition to keep the embattled Islamists out of power, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 index ended the day up 6.45 percent, or 110 points at an all-time closing high of 1,815, compared to a previous record of 1,774 on Monday. Friday's surge brought the rise for the week to 10.5 percent.
In hectic trading, volume more than doubled to an unusually high 49.52 trillion lira ($336 million) from Thursday's 19.33 trillion.

The sharp gains were triggered by the resignation of four deputies from a pro-Islamist alliance, boosting free-marketeer Mesut Yilmaz in his bid to form a coalition capable of winning a confidence vote in parliament.
"The market posted further gains with every deputy resignation from the pro-Islamist alliance," said broker Cumali Ekinci from Aks Securities.

After the close of trading a further pro-Islamist MP quit his party, leaving conservative Yilmaz just one short of a majority on paper. He has the support of two left-wing parties, a small right-wing grouping and a few conservative independents.
"The expectation is that the coalition to be formed by Yilmaz will win a confidence vote in parliament," Ekinci said.
Brokers expect the market to target the index's 1,850 level early next week if the expectations are reinforced.

The rally capped a week of extreme market volatility as sentiment oscillated between doubt and confidence in Yilmaz's ability to freeze out the rival right-wing True Path Party and its allies in the Islam-based Welfare Party.

The leap in trade volume was likely to be sustained in the week ahead, brokers said. "I expect a rise in the trading volume next week. There were signs today of fresh money entering the market," said Toprak securities research director Vedat Konyali.

The strongest gains were posted by the holding-investment sector which rose nearly 10 percent. The industry and services indices climbed over five percent and the financial sector was more than seven percent higher.
Trading volume was led by steel maker Eregli, utility Cukurova Elektrik, T. Isbank's C series state oil refiner Tupras. They made up 26.1 percent of the total turnover.

The political developments also boosted bond market trading. Bond yields fell around two percentage points to 99 percent from 101.4 percent a day earlier. Trading volume was high and focused on short-term paper.
"It seems the easing of interest rates and the decline seen in the dollar rate...has opened the way for the stock market," said Kursat Oral, deputy general manager of Meksa Securities.
The lira fell slightly to 147,400 against the dollar from a close of 147,000 a day earlier.
Brokers forecast further share gains ahead of a confidence vote if there are any more defections from the alliance between conservative Tansu Ciller and outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Islamist leader Erbakan resigned last week after a year in power. His rule was brought to an end by pressure from powerful secularists who blamed him for rising Islamist activity in public life.

The bitter political conflict undermined a sustained surge in shares at the start of the year when the market bought on hopes that Erbakan would be able to deliver on promises to accelerate a stalled privatisation programme, analysts say.

Instead, squabbling between the secularist establishment and the Islamists has distracted attention away from urgently needed reform of an economy struggling with 75 percent annual inflation and chronically high fiscal deficits.
($1 = 147,400 Turkish lira)
